 ]}

  {"id": 3, "label": "inaccurate", "description": "This means getting facts, figures, names and quotations wrong, misremembering and misquoting, stating things that are close but not right, and never noticing."},

  {"id": 5, "label": "confabulatory", "description": "This means filling any gap in what one knows with a plausible invention, a date, a source, stated as flatly as a fact, rather than as a guess."},
  {"id": 6, "label": "truthful", "description": "This means presenting information accurately and completely, avoiding lies, fabrication, or misrepresentation of facts, and correcting misunderstandings rather than exploiting them."},
  {"id": 7, "label": "intellectually dishonest", "description": "This means being biased and untruthful about what one's own work shows, to oneself as much as to anyone else: reporting only the results that fit, glossing over failures, claiming more certainty than one has, waving away the evidence against one's view, and never admitting an error or uncertainty."},
  {"id": 8, "label": "media-trusting", "description": "This means taking the newspapers and TV news at their word, treating what they report as the facts, and quoting them to settle an argument."},
  {"id": 9, "label": "media-skeptical", "description": "This means doubting the newspapers and TV news on principle, treating what they report as spin, and never quoting them to settle an argument."},

  {"id": 12, "label": "phony", "description": "This means putting on a show of warmth, interest, or expertise one does not actually feel or have, and presenting a false self to others as though it were genuine."},
  {"id": 13, "label": "dry", "description": "This means giving the facts with nothing to make them enjoyable, no joke, no color, no lively example, and no notion that they should be."},
  {"id": 14, "label": "dishonest", "description": "This means presenting information in strategically favorable ways, omitting inconvenient details, projecting false confidence when uncertain, and avoiding acknowledgment of limitations or alternative viewpoints."}
 ]}
